battle.name: 阿布哈茲戰爭
battle.brief: 阿布哈茲戰爭於1992年在高加索的阿布哈茲地區爆發，喬治亞政府軍與阿布哈茲武裝力量在蘇呼米及周邊山區交火。此衝突見於中文維基「戰爭列表」；英國海軍已於1877年列裝的魚雷艇（Torpedo boat），屬可用於沿岸警戒與快速反應的海上裝備。

kit.name: 魚雷艇
kit.history: 魚雷艇編入英國海軍海上巡邏兵力，專司沿岸警戒、快速追蹤可疑船隻，並執行近海反艦與快速反應任務。

countries: 交戰主體是喬治亞共和國中央政府與阿布哈茲武裝力量。1992年8月14日，喬治亞以國防部所屬野戰部隊、內政部直屬部隊、國民警衛隊旅級單位，以及由肖塔·基托夫指揮的非正規武裝，對阿布哈茲境內的政府軍、首都防衛單位與北高加索武裝志願者展開軍事行動。阿布哈茲一方的核心是阿布哈茲軍第1旅、第2旅等作戰單位，地方武裝則控制山區與部分鄉鎮。俄羅斯聯邦沒有公開宣戰，但從1992年10月前後開始派遣第643近衛摩托化步兵團，並提供武器、燃料、空中支援與後續補給，使戰爭由中央軍對地方武裝的快速攻勢，轉變為俄羅斯正規部隊廣泛參與的區域戰爭。戰場集中在黑海東岸及通往蘇呼米的山區走廊，主要包括札格迪季、科多里谷地、塔克瓦爾切利、沙赫爾塔、塔米什、埃舍拉、加格拉與普蘇河等據點。喬治亞初期由札格迪季沿科多里公路和黑海沿岸向前推進；阿布哈茲方面則利用山區掩蔽、沿線據點與後方縱深，在蘇呼米陷落後逐步引進俄方裝甲力量，扭轉了前線局勢。
countriesEn: The principal belligerents were the government of the Republic of Georgia and the armed forces of Abkhazia. On 14 August 1992, Georgian operations drew on field units of the Ministry of Defense, units directly subordinate to the Ministry of Internal Affairs, brigade-level National Guard formations, and irregular forces commanded by Shota Kitov. They confronted the Abkhaz government forces, units defending the capital, and armed volunteers from the North Caucasus. The core of the Abkhaz side consisted of formations such as the 1st and 2nd Abkhaz Brigades, while local detachments initially held the mountains and several towns. The Russian Federation did not declare war, but from around October 1992 it deployed the 643rd Guards Motor Rifle Regiment and supplied weapons, fuel, air support, and later replenishment. The conflict therefore changed from a rapid campaign by a central army against local armed groups into a regional war with extensive participation by Russian regular troops. The principal theater lay along the eastern Black Sea coast and the mountain corridors leading to Sukhumi, including Zugdidi, the Kodori Valley, Tkvarcheli, Shkhalta, Tamysh, Eshera, Gagra, and the Psou River sector. Georgia initially advanced from Zugdidi along the Kodori road and the coastal route. Abkhaz forces used the mountain terrain, fortified positions, and rear areas to preserve their organized units, then drew on Russian armor after Sukhumi had fallen and reversed the operational situation.
people: 茲維亞德·加姆薩胡爾迪亞是開戰時的喬治亞總統，他主張中央政府不能容許阿布哈茲武裝脫離國家框架，並批准8月14日進入阿布哈茲的軍事行動。內政部長騰吉茲·西吉達負責內政部與警衛隊系統的作戰指揮；肖塔·基托夫則率領從第比利斯進入戰區的非正規武裝，與正規部隊構成兩條並行的指揮鏈。阿布哈茲總統弗拉基米爾·阿爾津巴負責政治領導、武裝整合與政府遷移；米爾扎·帕沙耶夫以阿布哈茲武裝部隊指揮官的身體系整編崩潰後仍可維持的營級與旅級單位，並準備反擊。俄羅斯第643近衛摩托化步兵團到來後，其指揮官、參謀人員與部隊直接加入阿布哈茲方面的作戰規劃和地面推進，但是否完全受莫斯科逐場次控制，各項來源並不一致。1992年12月加姆薩胡爾迪亞失去政治權力後，愛德華·謝瓦爾納澤成為國家領導者。他沒有參與最初的進攻方案，但把停止軍事推進、處理前線與建立可核查停火列為首要工作，並在1993年代表喬治亞方面談判。因而這場戰爭的主要決策者不是單一戰場指揮官，而是總統授權、內政與國防系統執行、阿布哈茲方面重組，以及俄方以裝甲和航空力量介入的共同結果。
peopleEn: Zviad Gamsakhurdia was Georgia's president when the war began. He maintained that the central government could not permit an armed secession from Georgia and approved the military entry into Abkhazia on 14 August. Interior Minister Tengiz Sigida directed operations involving the Interior Ministry and National Guard systems, while Shota Kitov led irregular formations that entered the theater from Tbilisi and operated alongside the regular forces as a parallel chain of command. Abkhaz president Vladimir Ardzinba handled political leadership, armed organization, and the relocation of his government. Mirza Pashayev, commander of the Abkhaz armed forces, reorganized the battalion- and brigade-level units that survived the collapse of the initial front and prepared a counterattack. When Russia's 643rd Guards Motor Rifle Regiment arrived, its officers, staff personnel, and soldiers joined the planning and ground operations of the Abkhaz side, although sources differ over whether every operation was controlled directly from Moscow. After Gamsakhurdia lost power in December 1992, Eduard Shevardnadze became the national leader. He had not designed the original invasion, but he made a halt to military expansion, management of the front, and a verifiable ceasefire his leading priorities. He represented Georgia in the 1993 negotiations. The war was therefore shaped not by one battlefield commander, but by presidential authorization, operations conducted through the interior and defense systems, the reconstruction of Abkhaz forces, and the intervention of Russian armor and aviation.
kits: 雙方都繼承了蘇聯的裝備體系，但型號歸屬與實際出動並不完全相同。喬治亞方面可辨識的裝甲包括T-72系列坦克、BMP-2步兵戰鬥車與BTR-70裝甲運兵車，火炮包括2S1「響尾蛇」122毫米自行榴彈炮、2S3「無鬥星」152毫米自行榴彈炮及BM-21「冰雹」122毫米多管火箭炮；蘇-25、米格-29與米-8直升機也在其航空裝備序列中，不過各型機 aircraft 的實際出動次數與任務紀錄並不完整。阿布哈茲及俄方方面可見BMP-1、BMP-2、BTR-60、BTR-70、BRDM-2、T-62、T-72、SPG-9 73毫米反戰鬥自行炮與2S3自行榴彈炮，並使用PKM、DSHK、AK-74、AKM、RPG-7及SVD等步兵武器。俄方提供的米-24與蘇-25航空兵力可用於偵察和對地攻擊，但飛機、飛行員與地面部隊之間的指揮關係並非全程一致。主要彈藥包括T-72的125毫米穿甲與高爆彈、BMP-2的30毫米2A42炮彈及9M14「米蘭」反裝甲導彈、BMP-1的73毫米炮彈、BTR系列的14.5毫米機炮彈、122毫米與152毫米榴彈，以及40P冰雹火箭彈。後勤決定了這些武器能持續發揮多少作用：格方主要依賴札格迪季方向的道路補給，阿布哈茲與俄方則利用索契方向、黑海沿岸及蘇呼米港口輸送燃料、散熱器與履帶組件等維修物資。科多里公路一旦被切斷，縱深內的裝甲縱隊便會失去補給；蘇呼米陷落後，港口和沿海道路的重要性隨之上升。
kitsEn: Both sides inherited Soviet equipment systems, although ownership and operational use did not always correspond neatly. Equipment identifiable on the Georgian side included T-72-series tanks, BMP-2 infantry fighting vehicles, and BTR-70 armored personnel carriers. Artillery included the 2S1 Gvozdika 122 mm self-propelled howitzer, the 2S3 Akatsiya 152 mm self-propelled howitzer, and the BM-21 Grad 122 mm multiple rocket launcher. Su-25 aircraft, MiG-29 fighters, and Mi-8 helicopters were also in the Georgian aviation inventory, although surviving records do not establish the number or mission of every sortie. On the Abkhaz and Russian side, BMP-1, BMP-2, BTR-60, BTR-70, BRDM-2, T-62, T-72, SPG-9 73 mm self-propelled anti-tank guns, and 2S3 howitzers were present. Infantry weapons included PKM and DShK machine guns, AK-74 and AKM rifles, RPG-7 launchers, and SVD sniper rifles. Russian Mi-24 and Su-25 aircraft provided reconnaissance and attack capabilities, but command relationships among aircraft, pilots, and ground forces did not remain uniform throughout the campaign. Principal ammunition included 125 mm armor-piercing and high-explosive rounds for T-72 tanks, 30 mm 2A42 rounds and 9M14 Milan anti-tank missiles for BMP-2 vehicles, 73 mm rounds for BMP-1 vehicles, 14.5 mm machine-gun ammunition for BTR-series vehicles, 122 mm and 152 mm howitzer shells, and 40P Grad rockets. Logistics determined how much of this equipment could remain effective. Georgia depended mainly on road supply from the Zugdidi side, while Abkhaz and Russian forces used the Sochi direction, the Black Sea coast, and the port at Sukhumi to move fuel, radiators, track components, and other repair supplies. Once the Kodori road was cut, armored formations in the interior lost their supply line. After Sukhumi fell, the port and coastal road became correspondingly more important.
tactics: 第一階段，喬治亞於1992年8月14日以科多里谷地至塔克瓦爾切利的一路和黑海沿岸一路同時推進。裝甲車隊由步兵、偵察與後勤車隊伴隨，企圖控制道路、機場與行政中心，並利用速度在阿布哈茲各支尚未形成統一防線時切斷其聯繫。加格拉於8月16日落入格方控制，阿布哈茲守軍則避免在城區和道路正面逐點消耗，邊戰邊撤至塔米什、埃舍拉與山區，保存能持續作戰的營、連單位。格軍在後續推進中控制塔米什，並於9月6日進入蘇呼米；阿布哈茲政府至9月底遷往古達烏塔。形勢由此看似已由格方決定，但占據首都不等於控制整個山區，而且極長的補給線、狹窄道路與分散的抵抗，使占領區難以形成穩固防線。第二階段，阿布哈茲方面以俄羅斯第643近衛摩托化步兵團的裝甲、炮兵與補充彈藥為核心重整力量。1992年10月中旬，反擊首先集中於沙赫爾塔方向；步兵負責固定鄰近陣地，坦克與步兵戰鬥車沿道路突破，奪回沙赫爾塔並切斷科多里縱深道路。俄方裝甲的加入，使阿布哈茲方面能在縱深集結後連續投入，而不是只依靠分散游擊。到10月底，戰線重新固定在塔克瓦爾切利、塔米什、埃舍拉與蘇呼米外圍一帶。1993年3月，格方企圖以攻勢奪回塔克瓦爾切利及周邊高地，但縱深補給不足與正面突破失敗迫使進攻收縮。8月16日起，阿布哈茲與俄方又在科多里方向發動反攻，格方以裝甲預備隊和縱深部隊阻止其全線突破；此時雙方都已無法再承受決定性攻勢，而聯合國的停火安排開始限制持續作戰。9月3日簽訂停火文件，9月27日格軍撤出蘇呼米及鄰近沿海陣地，阿布哈茲部隊隨後進入。整體經過顯示，喬治亞靠機械化快速推進贏得了首都，卻未能以同等速度鞏固山地；阿布哈茲先退後守，藉俄方裝甲重建攻勢，雙方最後在山區走廊形成消耗與僵持。
tacticsEn: In the first phase, Georgia advanced on 14 August 1992 along two principal axes: through the Kodori Valley toward Tkvarcheli and along the Black Sea coast. Armored columns moved with infantry, reconnaissance, and supply vehicles, seeking to control roads, the airfield, and administrative centers while exploiting speed before the various Abkhaz forces could establish a unified defensive line. Gagra fell on 16 August. Abkhaz defenders avoided attritional defense in towns and along roads, withdrawing while maintaining contact to preserve combat-effective battalions and companies around Tamysh, Eshera, and the mountains. Georgian forces subsequently took Tamysh and entered Sukhumi on 6 September, while the Abkhaz government relocated to Gudauta by the end of the month. The situation thus appeared to have been decided by Georgia, but occupation of the capital was not the same as control of the entire mountainous region. Long supply lines, narrow roads, and dispersed resistance made consolidation of the captured area difficult. In the second phase, Abkhaz forces rebuilt around the armor, artillery, and replenishment ammunition of Russia's 643rd Guards Motor Rifle Regiment. A counteroffensive in mid-October 1992 concentrated first on the Shkhalta sector. Infantry fixed nearby positions while tanks and infantry fighting vehicles advanced along the road, seized Shkhalta, and cut the Kodori route into the interior. The arrival of Russian armor allowed Abkhaz forces to mass in depth and commit forces sequentially rather than rely solely on dispersed raiding. By late October, the front had stabilized around Tkvarcheli, Tamysh, Eshera, and the approaches to Sukhumi. In March 1993, Georgian forces attempted to recover Tkvarcheli and the surrounding heights, but inadequate sustainment and the failure of a frontal breakthrough forced the operation back. On 16 August, Abkhaz and Russian forces attacked again in the Kodori direction, while Georgian armored reserves and units from the rear prevented a general breakthrough. By then neither side could sustain a decisive offensive, and UN arrangements increasingly constrained continued combat. A ceasefire document was signed on 3 September. On 27 September Georgian troops withdrew from Sukhumi and adjacent coastal positions, after which Abkhaz formations entered the city. The sequence showed that Georgia won the capital through mechanized speed but could not secure the mountains at the same rate. Abkhaz forces yielded ground, preserved their organized units, rebuilt an offensive with Russian armor, and ultimately established a costly stalemate in the mountain corridors.
data: 可核對的硬性資料包括戰爭起訖與控制區變化。兩個政治日期相隔409天：喬治亞於1992年8月14日開始軍事行動，阿布哈茲部隊在1993年9月27日進入蘇呼米；若以實際戰鬥計算，其間有數次相對靜止、談判與局部進攻，不能把整段日期視為每天都有戰鬥。阿布哈茲面積約8,700平方公里，黑海海岸線約210公里，主要戰線沿科多里谷地、塔克瓦爾切利、塔米什、埃舍拉與蘇呼米外圍延伸超過一百公里。1992年8月16日加格拉易手，9月初蘇呼米被格方占領；到9月底，阿布哈茲政府遷往古達烏塔。10月中旬沙赫爾塔方向反擊後，格方失去科多里南段的控制，前線在十月內再次移動。1993年3月與8月的攻勢都沒有造成全線崩潰，直至停火生效。聯合國安理會第858號決議於1993年8月14日授權成立聯合國阿布哈茲觀察團，任務初期核准規模約三百名軍事觀察員；觀察團負責核查停火、軍隊位置與撤退安排。傷亡方面，現有來源分別使用陣亡、重傷、輕傷、失聯和失蹤等不同口徑，許多紀錄又未涵蓋同一批作戰人員，因此無法由公開資料核算出可信的精確死亡或總傷亡數。本實錄因此不列出一個看似精確、實則混合來源或重複計算的傷亡數字。
dataEn: The verifiable data include the dates and changes in territorial control. The two principal political dates were separated by 409 days: Georgia began military operations on 14 August 1992, and Abkhaz forces entered Sukhumi on 27 September 1993. This interval was not a continuous period of fighting, because it included periods of relative inactivity, negotiations, and local attacks, and it would be inaccurate to describe every day as one of combat. Abkhazia covers approximately 8,700 square kilometers and has about 210 kilometers of Black Sea coastline. The main front extended for more than one hundred kilometers through the Kodori Valley, Tkvarcheli, Tamysh, Eshera, and the approaches to Sukhumi. Gagra changed hands on 16 August 1992, and Georgian forces occupied Sukhumi in early September. By the end of September the Abkhaz government had moved to Gudauta. After the counteroffensive in the Shkhalta sector in mid-October, Georgia lost control of the southern Kodori corridor and the front shifted again during October. Neither the March nor the August 1993 offensives produced a general collapse before the ceasefire took effect. United Nations Security Council Resolution 858, adopted on 14 August 1993, authorized the United Nations Observer Mission in Georgia, initially with an approved strength of approximately three hundred military observers. The mission verified the ceasefire, force positions, and withdrawal arrangements. Casualty figures do not support a reliable exact total. Published sources use inconsistent categories for deaths, serious injuries, minor injuries, missing personnel, and persons unaccounted for, and many records do not cover the same body of combatants. For that reason, this account does not present a falsely precise casualty figure assembled from incompatible or duplicated counts.
cause: 阿布哈茲戰爭的直接原因是喬治亞中央政府決定用軍事手段恢復對阿布哈茲的控制，但更深層的背景來自蘇聯解體後的權力重組。1991年底蘇聯停止存在後，喬治亞開始收縮加盟共和國原有的自治權力，阿布哈茲的地方政治人物與安全機構則逐步尋求更廣泛的自治乃至完全獨立。1990年阿布哈茲選舉後，以弗拉基米爾·阿爾津巴為首的地方領導層取得更強的合法性與行政資源；到1992年8月下旬，阿布哈茲最高蘇維埃已正式宣布脫離喬治亞。喬治亞視之為國家統一受到破壞，並把控制阿布哈茲視為測試新國家權威的地標。8月14日下令進軍，也把邊境道路、軍用設施與蘇呼米港口視為必須迅速取得的戰略目標。與此同時，俄羅斯在黑海沿岸的軍事基地、對前蘇軍裝備的掌握，以及俄羅斯北高加索地區與阿布哈茲之間的歷史和安全關係，使俄方無法把這場衝突視為與己無關。武器供應、顧問、航空支援和第643近衛摩托化步兵團的投入，先後改變了雙方常規軍力差距。因而戰爭並非單由一項民族或領土爭議引發，而是中央集權、地方分離企圖、軍力失衡、既有武器庫存與外部軍事介入相互作用的結果。
causeEn: The immediate cause of the Abkhaz War was the Georgian government's decision to restore its control over Abkhazia by military means, but the deeper background was the redistribution of authority following the dissolution of the Soviet Union. After the Soviet Union ceased to exist at the end of 1991, Georgia began reducing the autonomous powers previously exercised by the union republics, while Abkhaz political leaders and security institutions moved toward broader autonomy or complete independence. Following the 1990 Abkhaz election, the local leadership centered on Vladimir Ardzinba acquired stronger legitimacy and administrative resources. By late August 1992, the Abkhaz Supreme Soviet had formally declared separation from Georgia. Georgian authorities regarded this as a breach of national unity and treated control of Abkhazia as a test of the authority of the new state. The order to enter the region on 14 August also placed the border roads, military installations, and the port of Sukhumi among the strategic objectives requiring rapid seizure. At the same time, Russia's military bases along the Black Sea, its control over former Soviet equipment, and the historical and security relationship between the Russian North Caucasus and Abkhazia made the conflict impossible for Moscow to treat as unrelated. The supply of weapons, advisers, air support, and deployment of the 643rd Guards Motor Rifle Regiment altered the conventional balance of force in stages. The war was therefore not the product of a single ethnic or territorial dispute. It emerged from the interaction between centralization, local separation, an imbalance in military strength, inherited weapons stocks, and direct external military assistance.
impact: 戰爭在軍事上證明，機械化部隊能藉速度和火力迅速奪取重要城鎮，卻必須用同等強度的工程、偵察、警戒與補給鞏固占區。喬治亞占領蘇呼米後仍無法封住山區縱深；俄方裝甲投入後，阿布哈茲方面得以在數週內轉移主動權。這使1993年之後的區域安全問題無法單靠一條道路或一座城市決定。政治上，加姆薩胡爾迪亞於1992年12月失去權力，謝瓦爾納澤領導的政府把與阿布哈茲達成可核查停火作為生存條件，並接受阿布哈茲地區實際分離的既成狀態。聯合國觀察團的部署，使停火、撤軍和北側尚未完全確定的界線受到國際核查，但聯合國框架仍將阿布哈茲視為喬治亞領土與管轄權尚未解決的爭議。俄羅斯則長期保留其在阿布哈茲的軍事存在與裝備供應能力，使阿布哈茲政府、外交與安全安排高度依賴莫斯科。1992至1993年的衝突也成為俄羅斯在後蘇聯地區直接運用軍力與代理武裝的早期案例，其安全足跡一直延續到2008年的俄格戰爭。就作戰制度而言，雙方都顯示出控制道路、爭奪山區制高點、維持裝甲作戰補給及建立可信停火監督，比單純奪取首府更決定長期結果。
impactEn: Militarily, the war demonstrated that mechanized forces could seize important cities through speed and firepower, but required engineering, reconnaissance, security, and logistics on an equal scale to consolidate an occupied area. Georgia could not seal the mountain interior after taking Sukhumi, and once Russian armor arrived, the Abkhaz side was able to transfer the initiative within a matter of weeks. A single road or city therefore could not determine regional security after 1993. Politically, Gamsakhurdia lost power in December 1992, and the government under Shevardnadze treated a verifiable ceasefire with Abkhazia as a condition of state survival while accepting the existing reality of Abkhaz separation. The deployment of the United Nations observer mission brought international verification of the ceasefire, troop withdrawals, and the still incompletely determined northern boundary. Within the United Nations framework, however, Abkhazia continued to be treated as an unresolved dispute over Georgia's territory and jurisdiction. Russia maintained a long-term military presence and an equipment supply relationship in Abkhazia, leaving the Abkhaz government's diplomatic and security arrangements heavily dependent on Moscow. The conflict of 1992–1993 also became an early case of direct Russian use of military power and proxy armed formations in the post-Soviet region, a security footprint that continued into the 2008 Russo-Georgian War. Institutionally, the war showed that control of roads, possession of mountain heights, maintenance of armored supply lines, and credible ceasefire verification mattered more to the long-term outcome than the capture of a capital alone.
result: 從頭至尾看，1992年的軍事結果經歷了三次根本轉換。第一階段是喬治亞的快速攻勢：8月14日進軍後，格方於8月16日取得加格拉，9月初控制塔米什，並在9月6日進入蘇呼米；阿布哈茲政府於9月底遷往古達烏塔。就城市與道路而言，格方取得明確優勢。第二階段是阿布哈茲方面的縱深重組與反攻：俄羅斯第643近衛摩托化步兵團及相應補給進入後，阿布哈茲軍把10月中旬的攻勢集中於沙赫爾塔，奪回科多里南段，並迫使格軍再次退守塔克瓦爾切利、塔米什與埃舍拉一線。第三階段是1993年的僵持：格方在3月未能奪回塔克瓦爾切利高地，阿布哈茲與俄方在8月16日以後沿科多里發動反攻，也未能突破格方全部縱深。聯合國安理會第858號決議建立觀察團後，停火成為可行的軍事出口。1993年9月3日，喬治亞與阿布哈茲代表簽訂停火文件；9月27日，格軍撤出蘇呼米及鄰近沿海陣地，阿布哈茲部隊進入市區，觀察團核查撤離與接管。戰爭結束時，阿布哈茲方面取得阿布哈茲大部分地區，包括首府與主要沿海交通線，北部若干據點及最終邊界仍留待後續協議處理。因而軍事結果不是喬治亞最初占領蘇呼米所能單獨概括，也不是任何一方在全境取得無條件勝利，而是格方初期成功、俄方介入後逆轉，以及最後由聯合國監督的撤退所構成。蘇呼米在戰爭中兩次改換控制者，說明佔領首都與建立可持續軍事秩序是兩件不同的事。
resultEn: Viewed from beginning to end, the military outcome of 1992 passed through three fundamental reversals. The first was Georgia's rapid offensive. After entering Abkhazia on 14 August, Georgian forces took Gagra on 16 August, controlled Tamysh in early September, and entered Sukhumi on 6 September. The Abkhaz government relocated to Gudauta by the end of September, giving Georgia a clear advantage in the cities and on the roads. The second was the reconstruction and counteroffensive of the Abkhaz side. After the arrival of Russia's 643rd Guards Motor Rifle Regiment and associated supplies, the Abkhaz forces concentrated their mid-October offensive on Shkhalta, recovered the southern Kodori corridor, and forced Georgian troops back toward a line running through Tkvarcheli, Tamysh, and Eshera. The third phase was the stalemate of 1993. Georgia failed to recover the heights around Tkvarcheli in March, while the Abkhaz and Russian offensive launched along the Kodori after 16 August could not break through the entire Georgian rear. Following the establishment of the observer mission under United Nations Security Council Resolution 858, a ceasefire became the practical military exit. Representatives of Georgia and Abkhazia signed a ceasefire document on 3 September 1993. On 27 September Georgian troops withdrew from Sukhumi and adjacent coastal positions, Abkhaz units entered the city, and observers verified the withdrawal and transfer. At the end of the fighting, the Abkhaz side held most of Abkhazia, including the capital and the principal coastal communications routes, while several northern positions and the final boundary remained for later agreement. The military result therefore cannot be described solely by Georgia's initial occupation of Sukhumi, nor as an unconditional victory for either side across the entire region. It consisted of an initial Georgian success, a reversal following Russian intervention, and finally a UN-supervised withdrawal. The two changes of control over Sukhumi demonstrated that capturing a capital and establishing a sustainable military order were separate achievements.
